subject.title: feat: expose ClawHub catalog feed lanes

question: Should ClawHub expose these root catalog feed lanes as public API now, and if so must they use the existing stored-publication feed contract before merge?
rationale: This changes public feed identity, client trust semantics, and unauthenticated read behavior; those are product/API boundary decisions rather than a narrow mechanical repair.

options.title: Require Stored Root Feed Publications
options.body: Move the new root lanes onto `catalogFeedPublications` or an equivalent cached, quota-protected publication path with distinct feed IDs before exposing public routes.

options.title: Approve Dynamic Root Lanes
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept request-time dynamic root feeds and the reviewed-lane attestation semantics after documenting the client-facing boundary.

options.title: Pause The Feed Stack
options.body: Keep the draft paused or close it if the cross-repository feed RFC and OpenClaw consumer contract are not ready to anchor ClawHub producer behavior.

recommendation.title: Require Stored Root Feed Publications
recommendation.body: Move the new root lanes onto `catalogFeedPublications` or an equivalent cached, quota-protected publication path with distinct feed IDs before exposing public routes.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has the most recent direct history on the hosted feed schema and contract documentation that defines the API boundary under review.
